title: Heredity
standard_text: Traits are passed from parents to offspring through genes on chromosomes; dominant and recessive alleles; Punnett squares predict the results of monohybrid crosses; incomplete dominance, codominance and sex-linked traits. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 1: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Life Science): genes and alleles, dominant and recessive traits, Punnett squares, incomplete and codominance and sex-linked traits. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Offspring get one allele from each parent.
body_html:
How to think about it

Genes on chromosomes carry the instructions for traits. Each person has two alleles for each gene, one from each parent. A dominant allele (T) shows when present; a recessive allele (t) shows only when there are two copies (tt).

A Punnett square predicts the offspring of a cross: Tt × Tt gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3 tall : 1 short. In incomplete dominance the heterozygote is in between (red × white gives pink); in codominance both show (blood type AB). Some traits are carried on the X chromosome.

Example

Tt × tt. Fraction with the recessive trait?

Punnett square

Answer: 1/2

Example

Genotype of a person with blood type O?

Recessive

Answer: ii

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dominant means more common.
  • Mixing up genotype and phenotype.
  • Forgetting that each parent gives only one allele.

faq.q: Why can two brown-eyed parents have a blue-eyed child?
faq.a: Both can carry a recessive allele and pass it on.

faq.q: Why is color blindness more common in males?
faq.a: The allele is on the X chromosome, and males have only one X.

items.q: Why are hemophilia and color blindness more common in males?
c: males have only one X chromosome, so one recessive allele shows its effect
items.e: Females are usually carriers.

items.q: Which disorder is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21)?
items.e: Down's syndrome: an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21).

items.q: What causes sickle-cell anemia?
c: an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)
lack of the enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine
a single base change making valine replace glutamic acid in β-globin
items.e: Sickle-cell anemia: a single base change making valine replace glutamic acid in β-globin.

items.q: What is the law of segregation?
c: the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation
items.e: Each gamete gets one allele.

items.q: Red-green color blindness is X-linked recessive. The mother is a carrier and the father is not color-blind. What is the chance a daughter is color-blind?
items.e: Sons get their X from their mother; daughters get one X from each parent.

items.q: Which disorder is caused by an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)?
items.e: Klinefelter's syndrome: an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY).

items.q: What causes Klinefelter's syndrome?

an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)
